---
title: Correlate
execute:
  warning: false
---


Cross-correlate a moving Ricker wavelet against one channel used as a virtual source.


## Example signal

```{python}
import dascore as dc

patch = dc.get_example_patch(
    "ricker_moveout",
    velocity=100,
    duration=2,
)

patch.viz.waterfall();
```

## Cross-correlation

Use channel 4 (zero-based index 3) as the virtual source. Its autocorrelation is at zero lag; channels on either side have negative or positive lags while retaining the 100 m/s moveout.

```{python}
corr = patch.correlate(distance=3, samples=True)
corr.squeeze().viz.waterfall();
```

## Normalized correlation

`normalize=True` divides each correlation by the square root of the trace's whole-trace energy times the source's, so the autocorrelation peaks at one and no value exceeds one in magnitude. The energies do not change with lag, so for traces with their mean removed this equals the Pearson coefficient only at zero lag.

```{python}
corr = patch.correlate(distance=3, samples=True, normalize=True)
corr.squeeze().viz.waterfall();
```
